pages.name: Introduction
pages.content: The Heads Up Poker benchmark is designed to evaluate the strategic reasoning of general-purpose large language models (LLMs) rather than specialized poker bots. Unlike perfect information games like chess, poker tests dynamic adaptation, resilience, opponent modeling, and deception (bluffing) in an environment with hidden information and random chance. This makes poker more closely resemble real-world decision-making where data is often incomplete and opposing actors may be actively misleading.

pages.name: Tournament
pages.content:
## Initial Seeding
Seeds are assigned according to our full leaderboard of 900,000 hands, with top-ranked models facing lower-ranked opponents to ensure a balanced bracket and prevent the two highest seeds from meeting before the final, should they win.

## Bracket Format
Winners are determined by average BB/100 (Big blinds per 100 hands) over 20,000 total hands. These matchups are organized as duplicative poker, wherein 10,000 hands are seeded and played by both models on opposite sides of the table. The model with the higher BB/100 at the end of 20,000 hands moves on. To keep each head-to-head clash within a reasonable livestream duration, videos will featured curated play highlighting model performance, but those selected hands do not alter the final outcome of the matchup.

## Tournament Stream
The streamed poker tournament and championship is based on head-to-head matchups from the full leaderboard of 900,000 hands. The final leaderboard will be based on 20,000 hands between *each* model pairing to generate a statistically robust ranking based on model scores and performance metrics. The full results will be released shortly after the event concludes.

During the gameplay, you’ll be able to see each of the models reasoning about their decisions. Gameplay speed is adjusted to ensure for an optimal viewing and commentating experience. Models have been asked to provide reasoning, and then to summarize their own reasoning for a more optimal viewing experience.

pages.name: Heads Up No Limit Texas Hold Em as a Benchmark
pages.content:
### Why It Matters
- The Heads-Up Poker Leaderboard provides a standardized framework for evaluating and comparing the game-theoretic reasoning and strategic adaptability of today’s general-purpose language models. In this benchmark, models compete in Heads-Up No-Limit Hold’em, a complex environment that requires reasoning under imperfect information.

- The harness relies strictly on text-based representations of the game state. Models must generate internal reasoning based on poker concepts rather than relying on visual pattern recognition or external tools.

- To mitigate the high variance inherent in card games, the benchmark uses a Hand Duplication methodology. The competition utilizes 10,000 pre-shuffled decks, where every model plays both sides of the same hand arrangements. While this does not eliminate luck entirely, it neutralizes unavoidable events such as pre-flop all-ins by ensuring they affect all models equally, allowing rankings to reflect strategic differences rather than chance.

### Harness and Structure
The poker environment is hosted on Kaggle and manages game initialization, state tracking, and termination when a hand or match ends or when illegal move limits are reached. All matches use a universal harness shared across all models to ensure fair comparison. Models are accessed via public APIs and operate solely on their existing knowledge, without access to external tools such as range calculators or odds sheets. The open-sourced harness code is available at: https://github.com/google-deepmind/game_arena


The harness consists of a prompt–parse–retry pipeline:
- A Prompt Builder provides a text-only description of the current game state and hand history, instructing models to play to maximize expected value and to justify their actions using poker concepts, without enumerating legal moves.
- A Response Parser converts model outputs into game actions, allowing one retry for invalid or illegal responses; repeated failure results in a forced check or fold, depending on the game state. A 60-minute timeout is enforced per play.
- A Sampler introduces controlled randomness via temperature settings to prevent repetitive play, meaning identical hands may yield different outcomes across runs.


### Evaluation
Model performance is evaluated through gameplay under the duplicated-hand setup described above. The use of shared hand sequences ensures that variance from card order impacts all models equally, enabling meaningful comparison of strategic performance across models.

### Additional Notes
- The benchmark relies on text-only interaction, requiring models to parse and reason about the game state from language descriptions.
- Models do not have access to external poker tools or solvers.
- The retry and fallback mechanism (check or fold) may affect outcomes for models that struggle with formatting or legality constraints.
- Despite duplication, poker remains a stochastic game, and variance is reduced but not eliminated.
